ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=128^\circ$, $P_{1}$ is the intersection point of the bisector of the interior angle $\angle ABC$ of $\triangle ABC$, which is $BP_{1}$, and the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle ACE$, which is $CP_{1}$. $P_{2}$ is the intersection point of the bisector of the interior angle $\angle P_{1}BC$ of $\triangle BP_{1}C$, which is $BP_{2}$, and the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle P_{1}CE$, which is $CP_{2}$. $P_{3}$ is the intersection point of the bisector of the interior angle $\angle P_{2}BC$ of $\triangle BP_{2}C$, which is $BP_{3}$, and the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle P_{2}CE$, which is $CP_{3}$. Continuing in this manner, what is the measure of $\angle P_{6}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the internal angle bisector BP and the external angle bisector CP1 of $\triangle ABC$ intersect at $P_{1}$,\\
hence, $\angle P_{1}BC = \frac{1}{2}\angle ABC$, $\angle P_{1}CE = \frac{1}{2}\angle ACE$,\\
since $\angle ACE = \angle A + \angle ABC$, $\angle P_{1}CE = \angle P_{1}BC + \angle P_{1}$,\\
thus, $\frac{1}{2}(\angle A + \angle ABC) = \angle P_{1}BC + \angle P_{1} = \frac{1}{2}\angle ABC + \angle P_{1}$,\\
therefore, $\angle P_{1} = \frac{1}{2}\angle A = \frac{1}{2} \times 128^\circ = 64^\circ$,\\
similarly, $\angle P_{2} = \frac{1}{2}\angle P_{1} = 32^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle P_{6} = \boxed{2^\circ}$,

method.method_draft: Use directed ray angles relative to the base line BCE. From the image, take BCE as a straight horizontal baseline, with rays BP_i and CP_i above it; the desired ∠P_i is the difference between the directions of the ray from B to P_i and the ray from C to P_i. From the text, let ∠ABC=x. Since ∠BAC=128°, the exterior angle at C satisfies ∠ACE=x+128°. Because BP1 bisects ∠ABC, the direction of BP1 above BC is x/2. Because CP1 bisects exterior ∠ACE, the direction of CP1 above CE is (x+128°)/2. Therefore ∠P1=[(x+128°)/2]-x/2=64°. For the next step, BP2 halves the previous B-side direction, so its direction is x/4; CP2 halves the previous C-side exterior direction, so its direction is (x+128°)/4. Hence ∠P2=[(x+128°)/4]-x/4=32°. In general, BP_n has direction x/2^n and CP_n has direction (x+128°)/2^n, so ∠P_n=128°/2^n. Thus ∠P6=128°/64=2°.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=128^\circ$, $P_{1}$ is the intersection point of the bisector of the interior angle $\angle ABC$ of $\triangle ABC$, which is $BP_{1}$, and the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle ACE$, which is $CP_{1}$. $P_{2}$ is the intersection point of the bisector of the interior angle $\angle P_{1}BC$ of $\triangle BP_{1}C$, which is $BP_{2}$, and the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle P_{1}CE$, which is $CP_{2}$. $P_{3}$ is the intersection point of the bisector of the interior angle $\angle P_{2}BC$ of $\triangle BP_{2}C$, which is $BP_{3}$, and the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle P_{2}CE$, which is $CP_{3}$. Continuing in this manner, what is the measure of $\angle P_{6}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the internal angle bisector BP and the external angle bisector CP1 of $\triangle ABC$ intersect at $P_{1}$,\\
hence, $\angle P_{1}BC = \frac{1}{2}\angle ABC$, $\angle P_{1}CE = \frac{1}{2}\angle ACE$,\\
since $\angle ACE = \angle A + \angle ABC$, $\angle P_{1}CE = \angle P_{1}BC + \angle P_{1}$,\\
thus, $\frac{1}{2}(\angle A + \angle ABC) = \angle P_{1}BC + \angle P_{1} = \frac{1}{2}\angle ABC + \angle P_{1}$,\\
therefore, $\angle P_{1} = \frac{1}{2}\angle A = \frac{1}{2} \times 128^\circ = 64^\circ$,\\
similarly, $\angle P_{2} = \frac{1}{2}\angle P_{1} = 32^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle P_{6} = \boxed{2^\circ}$,
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: Both attached figures show the same geometric configuration: point B is at the lower left, point C is at the lower right, and BC is extended rightward to E; point A is above, forming triangle ABC with B and C. In the figure, from B there are multiple rays respectively connected to P1, P2, P3, and from C there are also line segments connected to P1, P2, P3; P1, P2, P3 are located in an area to the upper right of C, indicating that the angle at each Pi is the angle formed by BPi and CPi, namely ∠BP_iC. Reasoning: First prove the iterative angle-tracking lemma. Suppose in triangle BQC, the bisector of the interior angle ∠QBC at B and the bisector of the exterior angle ∠QCE at C intersect at R. Because CE is the extension line of BC, the exterior angle ∠QCE = ∠QBC + ∠BQC. Also because BR bisects ∠QBC, and CR bisects ∠QCE, ∠RBC = 1/2∠QBC, ∠RCE = 1/2∠QCE. In triangle BRC, ∠RCE is the exterior angle at C, therefore ∠RCE = ∠RBC + ∠BRC. Thus ∠BRC = ∠RCE - ∠RBC = 1/2∠QCE - 1/2∠QBC = 1/2(∠QCE - ∠QBC) = 1/2∠BQC. Therefore the newly obtained angle at each step equals half of the angle from the previous step. For the first time take Q=A, obtaining ∠P1 = 1/2∠BAC = 64°. Continue iterating: ∠P2 = 32°, ∠P3 = 16°, ∠P4 = 8°, ∠P5 = 4°, ∠P6 = 2°.
